episodes.188403: An atmospheric river moving through the Aleutians on March 19th - March 21nd dropped heavy rain of 3-5 inches storm total over the Onalaska/Dutch Harbor area. The heavy rain came in 2 strong pulses, one on 3/19 of up to 3 which started flooding in the area, with a  second pulse overnight on 3/21 which exacerbated flooding in the area.
episodes.190126: A cutoff upper-level low was situated over the Lower Colorado River Valley area on the 18th, bringing some unsettled weather to parts of south-central Arizona. SBCAPE in excess of 500 J/kg along with steep mid-level lapse rates led to thunderstorms producing hail around 0.75. No damage was reported with these thunderstorms.
episodes.190254: A cold front pushed southeast across the Chesapeake Bay late on the night of March 18th into March 19th, causing gusty winds.
episodes.190468: A tornado was observed at Little Torch Key as rapid development of showers and thunderstorms occurred directly over the Lower and Middle Florida Keys.  A cold front was approaching from the north, with the thunderstorms development over a pre-existing convergence boundary just as northerly surface winds were spreading over the Florida Keys.

A brief tornado was determined to have passed from State Road 4A through Diane Avenue and Linda Street on the northern portion of Little Torch Key.  The narrow path was marked by two downed buttonwood trees, broken small and medium-sized tree branches, a destroyed plastic storage shed, and three destroyed breakaway shade canopies.  No structural damage was observed.  Estimated maximum winds were 65 to 70 mph.

Unalaska Roads Department reported heavy rain in Unalaska washed out several gravel roadways in the surrounding area.  Blocked culverts caused additional street flooding and also washed large crevasses up to 4 ft deep in some of the roadways.
